Mesh3d lighting objects

Source: R/zz-gen-mesh3d.R
go_mesh3d_lighting.Rd

The object for the lighting of a mesh3d trace (go_mesh3d()). go_mesh3d_lighting() creates one, with exactly its properties; a named list with the same properties works too.

Usage

go_mesh3d_lighting(
  arg = NULL,
  ...,
  ambient = NULL,
  diffuse = NULL,
  facenormalsepsilon = NULL,
  fresnel = NULL,
  roughness = NULL,
  specular = NULL,
  vertexnormalsepsilon = NULL,
  skip_invalid = FALSE
)

Arguments

arg

Optional named list, or graph object of the same type, to initialise properties from. Named arguments take precedence.

...

Not used: properties must be named in full.

ambient

Ambient light increases overall color visibility but can wash out the image. Number in the interval [0, 1].

diffuse

Represents the extent that incident rays are reflected in a range of angles. Number in the interval [0, 1].

facenormalsepsilon

Epsilon for face normals calculation avoids math issues arising from degenerate geometry. Number in the interval [0, 1].

fresnel

Represents the reflectance as a dependency of the viewing angle; e.g. paper is reflective when viewing it from the edge of the paper (almost 90 degrees), causing shine. Number in the interval [0, 5].

roughness

Alters specular reflection; the rougher the surface, the wider and less contrasty the shine. Number in the interval [0, 1].

specular

Represents the level that incident rays are reflected in a single direction, causing shine. Number in the interval [0, 2].

vertexnormalsepsilon

Epsilon for vertex normals calculation avoids math issues arising from degenerate geometry. Number in the interval [0, 1].

skip_invalid

If TRUE, silently drop invalid properties instead of raising an error.

Value

A go_mesh3d_lighting object (a named list).

Details

Nested objects are named lists, or objects of the constructors their arguments name. Every property is checked against the plotly.js schema when the object is created or modified. A property may be a one-sided formula (color = ~col): it is kept, and evaluated in the data (then checked) when its trace is added to a figure with add_<trace>() or add_trace().

Examples

mtcars |>
  go_figure() |>
  add_mesh3d(
    x = ~wt,
    y = ~hp,
    z = ~mpg,
    lighting = go_mesh3d_lighting()
  )
